Name: John Chrysostom
Summary: Archbishop of Constantinople around the turn of the fifth century, called Chrysostom, meaning golden-mouthed, for his preaching.
Contribution: His plain, practical sermons expounded whole books of the Bible verse by verse and called rich and poor alike to repentance and generosity; his liturgy is still used in Eastern Orthodox worship today.
KeyWorks: Homilies on Matthew, John, and Romans; On the Priesthood
Testimony: Preached fearlessly against luxury and corruption, accepting exile twice rather than softening his message.
